Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

1) basic service / older notes
Morrow Table is an independent weekly meal subscription serving the east side of Bellwether and the nearby towns of Larch Point and Fen Ferry. It started in March 2023 with 42 households. The latest sheet, dated 7 October 2024, lists 318 active households, but that number means accounts that placed an order in the previous 30 days, not everybody who has ever subscribed. The team has six full-time staff and hires two kitchen assistants on Thursday and Friday. Their prep kitchen is in a converted print shop on Alder Street; there’s no dining room or walk-in ordering. Each week, customers choose three, four, or five dinners for one or two people. The meals arrive chilled, not frozen, with reheating cards. There’s a separate family box being tested, but it isn’t a standard plan yet.

2) menu and food details
The menu changes every Tuesday for the following delivery week. The regular rotation has included lemon lentil stew, miso-glazed salmon, mushroom barley pie, and chicken with preserved lemon. Those are examples from recent menus, not promises that any dish will come back. The kitchen labels common allergens on each menu and says its prep area handles milk, eggs, wheat, soy, fish, and sesame. It cannot promise that a meal is free from cross-contact. A September customer note said, “I liked the food, but the lentil stew needed more salt.” Staff replied that seasoning feedback was being passed to the kitchen; there’s no note saying the recipe was changed. The salmon was temporarily removed in August when the supplier could not confirm the harvest area for one delivery. It returned two weeks later after the supplier provided the paperwork. Don’t imply the salmon is permanently removed or that all fish sourcing has been verified.

3) plans, price and ordering
The 7 October price sheet lists $48 for three dinners for one, $76 for three dinners for two, and $62 for four dinners for one. Five-dinner plans are available, but the note doesn’t give their price. Delivery costs $6 inside Bellwether and $9 to Larch Point or Fen Ferry; the fee is waived on orders above $110. There is no charge listed for collection at the kitchen, but collection is only offered on Friday between 4 and 6 p.m. Orders close Sunday at 8 p.m. Customers can skip or cancel online until that deadline, and the notes say the account is charged when the order closes. 4) delivery and packaging
Routes go out Thursday afternoon in a two-hour window selected at checkout. Drivers text when they are about 20 minutes away. Orders are left at the door unless a customer selects handoff, and the team asks customers to add a cooler note if they will be out. The notes record 11 late deliveries in September out of 276 orders, mostly due to road work on the Fen Ferry route. One box arrived warm on 19 September; support refunded that box and logged a temperature check with the driver. The notes don’t say whether the check found a wider problem. Packaging is mostly recyclable cardboard, but the insulated liner and two cold packs are not accepted in Bellwether’s curbside collection. Customers can bring those items back at Friday collection; so far, 37 liners have been returned since June. The company has talked about a return bag for delivery customers, but that’s a proposal only.

5) customer feedback and support
A survey sent to 90 recent customers got 34 replies. Twenty-six respondents said the portions were about right, five wanted larger portions, and three did not answer that question. Twenty-one said menu variety was good; nine asked for more vegetarian dinners, and four skipped the question. These are counts from replies, not from all subscribers. The notes quote one respondent: “I want more meals I can freeze when work gets busy.” The kitchen currently advises eating meals within four days and doesn’t claim they freeze well. Support is staffed by one coordinator from Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. Replies outside those hours wait until the next workday. The team logged 63 support contacts in September, with delivery timing and skipping an order as the two most common topics; no breakdown by topic is included.

6) operating notes and possible changes
Ingredient costs were 8 percent higher in September than in April, according to the purchasing spreadsheet. A staff note says the kitchen is checking whether a larger lentil order could lower costs, but there’s no decision or savings estimate. The family box test ran for four weeks with 18 households. Notes say families liked the larger tray, but two households said the portion still wasn’t enough for four adults. The test ended on 27 September, and the team has not decided whether to offer the box regularly. A second delivery van is being considered for winter; the notes give no purchase date, budget, or approval. The company has confirmed a holiday pause on deliveries from 23 December through 2 January. Customers with an active plan will need to choose a delivery before the pause or skip those weeks. A draft email is being prepared, but it has not been sent.

Please use a clear title and numbered sections, with the same subject order as the notes where practical. Summarize the supplied notes rather than writing a sales page or an opinion piece.
